title: Joint response reliability left a similarity slope change uncertain after cell controls in one MICrONS mouse
abstract: We tested whether the product of two response correlation ceilings changes the relation between measured movie response similarity and synaptic connection. Public MICrONS v1 tables linked activity and anatomy in one mouse. The candidate panel had 295,371 ordered pairs and 8,128 connections. A Poisson mean model with source and target cell effects used 163,870 informative pairs. The interaction coefficient was 0.0265, with a nominal shared-cell 95% interval of -0.0011 to 0.0541. The test left the slope change uncertain. The response-quality interval was just above zero; different-scan and extra-geometry intervals included zero. This is a follow-up to prior reliability analyses, with joint reliability and both cell effects. One animal, selected cells, measurement error and a mean model that can exceed one limit inference. Code, scalar data, fitted outputs, checks and a static figure support reproduction.

display.caption: Joint response reliability and the similarity slope. Bars show nominal 95% intervals with shared-cell dependence. All fits use the same global scales. One mouse supplies all data.

citations.reason: Prior main reliability and target-reliability slope tests. This study tests joint reliability with both cell effects in one mouse.
Reuse profile Poisson code, validation code and data retrieval recipe. New scalar data preparation and reliability test.
